questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to promulgate Ordinances during the recess of Parliament?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Article 123 grants the President of India the power to promulgate Ordinances when either of the two Houses of Parliament is not in session, and he is satisfied that immediate action is required. These ordinances have the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament.
DECOY BUSTING: Article 213 gives the exact same power to the GOVERNOR of a state. Article 143 is the President's power to consult the Supreme Court. Article 356 is President's Rule.
EXAM INSIGHT: An ordinance must be approved by Parliament within 6 weeks of its reassembly. Since the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament can be 6 months, the maximum life of an ordinance is 6 months + 6 weeks.

questions.stem: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: According to Article 64 of the Constitution, the Vice-President of India acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). This means whoever holds the office of Vice-President automatically becomes the presiding officer of the Upper House.
DECOY BUSTING: The President does not sit in Parliament. The Prime Minister is a member of either house but does not preside. 
EXAM INSIGHT: Unlike the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (who is an elected member of the Lok Sabha), the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is NOT a member of the house he presides over. Therefore, he cannot vote in the first instance, but can cast a deciding vote in case of a tie.
